name: Zentech Manufacturing, Inc.
old_description: Waleid is responsible for Quality and Manufacturing Engineering at Zentech. He has over 20 years experience in manufacturing and prior to joining Zentech had extensive experience in the printed circuit board fabrication industry as a Quality Engineer and Quality Manager. Waleid has a BS in Electronics Engineering Technology from Southeastern Oklahoma State University and has been with Zentech since 2004.
about:
Zentech Manufacturing, Inc. was founded in 1998 and is headquartered in Baltimore, Maryland, with additional facilities in Richardson, Texas, and Bloomington, Illinois. The company operates as an electronic manufacturing services (EMS) provider specializing in high-reliability, high-complexity assemblies for mission-critical applications.

The company delivers full-turnkey electronic manufacturing services, including printed circuit board assembly (PCBA), system-level assembly and integration, comprehensive inspection and testing, higher-level assembly (HLA), new product introduction (NPI), program management, test development, and supply chain services. Zentech operates 180,000 square feet of manufacturing space across three sites, equipped with 11 surface-mount technology (SMT) lines, and focuses on low-to-medium volume, high-mix production of complex, high-reliability assemblies compliant with IPC 610 Class 2 and Class 3 standards.

Zentech serves primarily the defense and aerospace sector, which accounts for approximately 85 percent of its business, along with medical device manufacturers (10 percent) and commercial/industrial clients (5 percent). Its assemblies are used in mission-critical applications that protect national infrastructure and warfighters, though specific customer names are not disclosed.

Zentech emphasizes its comprehensive certification portfolio—including AS9100, ISO 13485, ITAR registration, IPC 610 Source Supplier, IPC J-STD-001 Space Addendum, and IPC 1791 Assembler—as a key differentiator for high-reliability medical and military circuit card assemblies. The company also highlights its in-house engineering team, including electro-mechanical designers, electrical design engineers, and test engineers, as a distinction from typical contract manufacturers.

name: 4 B Plastics Inc
old_description: We have been doing business with 4B Plastics since 1982.  We have always received excellent workmanship and service. They have extensive knowledge of different ball valves and seat design. Whether we need a same day turn-around or standard delivery, they have been able to accommodate our needs.
about:
4 B Plastics Inc operates from Baton Rouge, Louisiana, where it was founded in 1982. The company is led by Steven Braud, who heads a team of master machinists and technicians. Since its start, the business has focused on supplying high-quality PTFE components and custom-machined parts to industrial customers.

The company compression-molds its own unfilled and filled PTFE rod and tube stock, maintaining control from billet to finished part. Its shop custom machines OEM replacement parts — including lantern rings, compressor rings, V-rings, valve repair kits, bushings, bearings, seals, gaskets, and spacers — to customer specifications, often delivering in days. 4 B Plastics also stocks and sells the raw PTFE and specialty thermoplastic materials for customers who machine their own parts.

Primary customers are chemical plants, paper mills, and valve repair shops across the U.S. and abroad. The company supports international projects and corrosion-control systems worldwide, with testimonials citing 24/7 emergency supply during plant turnarounds. Technicians review specs and drawings alongside client project managers to coordinate timely delivery and export logistics.

4 B Plastics differentiates itself with same-day rush capability, in-house PTFE molding for quality assurance, and a master-machinist team that can turn custom orders around in days rather than weeks. Customers highlight competitive pricing and the ability to respond to middle-of-the-night or weekend emergencies that prevent costly downtime.

name: 4G Steel Fabrication
old_description: 4G Steel Fabrication is a mid-sized steel fabrication company located in the center of Americas heartland – Lincoln, Nebraska. Working on the cusp of steel fabrication with the use of leading technologies in our field of work to provide our customers with a product built with quality in mind.
about:
4G Steel Fabrication operates from Lincoln, Nebraska, in the center of the American heartland. The company was launched in February 2015 by four partners — the “4 Guys” behind the name — and is now owned and operated by two of the original founders, Charlie Fleck and Tim Limon. Their goal was to build the most efficient and productive structural steel fabrication business in the region while creating a workplace where employees could build long-term careers with strong benefits.

The shop specializes in structural and miscellaneous steel fabrication for commercial and institutional projects. Recent work includes the 925-ton Canopy Park in Lincoln, 887 tons for the University of Nebraska’s Mabel Lee Hall, 810 tons for Wichita State University’s Woolsey Hall, 495 tons for SCC Health Sciences, 322 tons for ICM in Colwich, Kansas, and 263 tons for Summerland Schools in Ewing, Nebraska. The company emphasizes the use of current fabrication technologies to maintain quality across projects of varying scale.

Primary customers are in education, healthcare, public infrastructure, and industrial construction. Project owners include public universities, school districts, healthcare systems, and municipal developments across Nebraska and Kansas.

Leadership points to more than 49 years of combined industry experience as the foundation for efficient management, on-time delivery, and craftsmanship that meets project specifications. The ownership model is designed to retain skilled workers through retirement-eligible benefits, which the founders say translates into consistent quality for clients.

name: 701 Sawmill
old_description: With a decade of experience, 701 Sawmill has helped countless customers across North Dakota turn their vision into stunning live edge slab projects. Whether you bring your own log or choose from our large selection of locally milled hardwoods, we’ll custom cut and craft each piece to highlight its natural beauty. From kitchen islands and tables to mantels and countertops, we take pride in creating quality woodwork that stands the test of time.
about:
701 Sawmill operates from Mandan, North Dakota, where it was established in 2016. The company focuses on custom wood milling and live‑edge slab production for customers across the northern Plains.

The shop cuts and dries a rotating inventory of more than 200 live‑edge slabs, sourced from locally harvested hardwoods. Logs brought in by customers are milled to specification on professional‑grade equipment, then kiln‑dried to 8 percent moisture content and flattened on a planer. The output ranges from raw slabs to finished furniture pieces such as tables, countertops, mantels, and shelves. New slabs are continuously added as stock sells, ensuring a broad selection of species and dimensions.

Clients include DIY woodworkers, professional contractors building homes, and craftsmen working on custom projects throughout North Dakota, South Dakota, and Montana. The company serves both residential and light commercial woodworking needs.

Founded on a decade of hands‑on experience, 701 Sawmill emphasizes the natural character of each log, aiming to deliver woodwork that withstands long‑term use.

about:
Founded in 1993 in the Bronx, New York, A & L Sheet Metal Fabrications has operated as a sheet metal fabrication shop for over three decades. The company began as a local provider of custom metalwork and has since expanded its capabilities to serve a range of industrial clients.

The shop offers a full suite of sheet metal processes: shearing, punching, laser cutting, bending, drilling and tapping, welding and spot welding, tool and die making, and machining. These services are performed in-house, allowing the company to handle projects from prototype through production runs without outsourcing core operations.

A & L primarily serves the defense and aerospace sectors, supplying fabricated components that meet stringent quality requirements. Its customer base also includes other industrial manufacturers requiring precision sheet metal parts for assemblies and enclosures.

The company emphasizes a distinguished level of service and the integration of cutting‑edge technology as its key differentiators. It maintains an ISO 9001:2008 certified quality management system, which it cites as essential to meeting customer timetables and delivering consistent results.

name: A & N Custom Fabrication Inc
old_description: Vegas Custom Fabrication has been the vendor of choice for many companies and individuals since 1977. We currently supply metal fabricated assemblies and services for customers throughout the Las Vegas valley including Las Vegas, North Las Vegas, Sunrise Mountain, Nellis, Green Valley, Henderson, Boulder City, and Summerlin.  We serve the construction, manufacturing, hospitality, government, gaming and a variety of other industries for over 30 years!
about:
Vegas Custom Fabrication, operating in Las Vegas, Nevada, traces its roots to 1977 when A & N Fabrication opened just west of the Las Vegas Strip. The second-generation, family-owned shop was taken over by Ron Nelson in August 2026, continuing a legacy of serving casinos, construction firms, and government agencies such as Clark County.

The company specializes in heavy-duty press brake forming with machines ranging from 50 to 1,500 tons, allowing complex parts to be produced in a single piece without splice welding. In-house capabilities include waterjet cutting, sand blasting, painting, punching, and precision welding — flux-core arc (FCAW), gas metal arc (GMAW/MIG), and gas tungsten arc (GTAW/TIG) — on aluminum, carbon steel, stainless steel, and T1 and Domex alloys. Powder coating is sourced through long-standing vendor partners. The shop handles both one-off prototypes and large production runs.

Customers span construction, manufacturing, hospitality, gaming, and government sectors. Typical output includes custom steel bollards, brackets, frames, guards, job boxes, ladder racks, machine and robot bases, material storage solutions, panels, racks, service boxes, tables, jacketed and non-jacketed tanks, welded components, weldments, wire troughs, and wireways.

The firm emphasizes quick turn-around, competitive pricing, and worldwide shipping, positioning its versatility and caring customer service as key differentiators. By consolidating multiple operations under one roof, it aims to reduce assembly time and material waste for clients.

name: A&A Manufacturing
old_description: At A&A Manufacturing, we build and supply the chassis components racers and fabricators trust. Family-owned since 1966 in Spring Lake, Michigan, we manufacture roughly 90% of our parts in-house and source the remainder locally—so you get consistent quality, tight tolerances, and dependable availability from a single, responsive chassis parts supplier.
about:
A&A Manufacturing has operated from Spring Lake, Michigan since its founding in 1966. The family‑owned business began with a simple goal: produce hard‑to‑find chassis tabs, mounts, and hardware domestically so racers and fabricators could focus on building better vehicles.

The company manufactures a range of chassis components for racing and off‑road applications, including suspension mounts, shock mounts, engine and transmission mounts, braking hardware, gussets, fasteners, and heim joints. Roughly 90 % of the catalog is produced in‑house using precision stamping, laser cutting, machining, and fabrication; the balance comes from local partners. A single facility houses both production and a walk‑in showroom, and in‑stock orders can ship same‑day nationwide.

Customers include race teams, hot‑rod builders, off‑road enthusiasts, professional technicians, and fabrication shops — anyone who needs weld‑ready components with consistent fitment. The shop also supports DIY racers and technician shops with custom one‑off or short‑run tabs, brackets, and specialty mounts, offering guidance on material selection and design trade‑offs.

A&A emphasizes domestic manufacturing as a differentiator: controlling materials, tolerances, and finish in its own shop yields repeatable hole sizing, bend accuracy, and weld‑ready edges. Local sourcing for the remaining items allows quick scaling of specialty runs without compromising quality, and the team provides responsive support from people who know the parts because they make them.

name: A.C. Legg, Inc.
old_description: A.C. Legg has proudly served the meat industry since 1923. We believe in quality, consistency, service, and quick response to achieve the greatest customer satisfaction possible. Our philosophy of excellence will never be compromised.
about:
A.C. Legg, Inc. was founded in 1923 in Birmingham, Alabama, by A.C. Legg, who crafted a secret-recipe pork sausage seasoning at his downtown meat market. In 1936, Charles W. Purvis joined the company as an office employee, later acquiring ownership and establishing a family-owned legacy that continues today under CEO James E. Purvis and his grandchildren. The company is now headquartered in Calera, Alabama.

The company manufactures custom seasoning blends and spice packaging for the meat and food processing industries. Its product portfolio includes a signature line of sausage seasonings rooted in the original Southern Style recipe, as well as custom formulations developed to exact customer specifications through a specialized blending and packaging process.

A.C. Legg serves commercial food processors, custom processors, grocery stores, deer processors, butcher shops, food service operations, and hobbyists, with a primary focus on the meat industry.

The company emphasizes quality, consistency, service, and quick response to achieve customer satisfaction, guided by a vision to develop and produce the highest quality customized seasoning solutions.

name: A.F. Johnson Millwork Co.
old_description: A.F. Johnson Millwork Company has delivered architectural millwork excellence for nine decades. As an AWI Premium Quality Certified member since 1989, we bring unmatched expertise to commercial projects nationwide. Our West Des Moines facility houses 25 skilled professionals, including designers, CNC experts, and master cabinetmakers, using advanced Microvellum and AutoCAD technology.
about:
A.F. Johnson Millwork Co. has operated from West Des Moines, Iowa since its founding in 1932 by Swedish immigrant Adolph F. Johnson. The company remains family-owned, with Johnson's son Richard "Dick" Johnson joining the business and passing the same exacting standard to subsequent generations. What began as a shop building out national chain stores across the Midwest grew into a dedicated architectural millwork facility.

The 25-person team — designers, engineers, CNC programmers, and master cabinetmakers — produces custom architectural millwork, casework, solid-surface fabrications, and upholstered seating. Work flows through a single West Des Moines plant equipped with CNC machining centers, Microvellum manufacturing software, and AutoCAD drafting, handling projects valued from $50,000 to seven figures. Services span concept development, detailed 3D renderings, fabrication, finishing, and nationwide installation.

Primary markets include retail, corporate, hospitality, healthcare, education, religious, and government sectors. The firm collaborates directly with architects, designers, and general contractors on commercial projects that represent roughly 95 percent of its workload, with select high-end residential commissions rounding out the portfolio.

The company cites its AWI Premium Quality Certification (held since 1989), nine decades of continuous operation, and the integration of advanced digital tools with traditional craftsmanship as its core differentiators. Every project carries a full one-year warranty per AWI specifications, backed by multiple in-process quality checkpoints.
